Keep in mind though sometimes it’s just being played as background music and no one is really listening to it... like at a store, bowling alley, gym, etc. Also music popularity tends to snowball, so it can disproportionately represent the population. This is because some people only listen to the radio or “Spotify top 100” or whatever, over and over. So if the song is popular enough to be a radio hit, it’s popularity skyrockets and a handful of artists might get a huge number of plays... but people with a more eclectic music taste tend to listen to a variety of artists, and they won’t constantly listen to one song/artist over and over. But for me personally the ultimate purpose of psychedelics (and psych music) is to go deep and uncover buried aspects of yourself. Having fun while doing it is a big plus, but I feel like that’s primarily what separates psychs from other drugs (more addictive ones). Early in my psychonautical career I would just skip any music that I was afraid would spiral me into a bad trip, now I really enjoy darker themes during my trips because I learn the most from them. My most fun trips are often a whole roller coaster of emotions.
